title: Constrain preflight projectName to a UE project identifier
body:
## Summary
POST /api/packaging/preflight accepts any string as projectName and splices it into the .uproject path and the UBT target argument.

## Description
src/app/api/packaging/preflight/route.ts:44 only checks typeof projectName === "string". runBuildVerify (route.ts:62) builds `${projectName}.uproject` under projectPath and passes `${projectName}Editor` as the first UBT argument; runAssetValidation (route.ts:80) and the target at route.ts:122 does the same. A name containing `..\` resolves a .uproject outside projectPath, and a name starting with `-` is parsed by UBT as a flag. No shell is involved (spawn without shell), so this is argument/path confusion, not command injection. Fixed = reject names outside UE's project-name alphabet (letters, digits, underscore) with 400 before spawning.

## Flow
- POST {projectName:"..\\..\\Other\\Game", check:"build-verify-editor"}
- route joins projectPath + "..\\..\\Other\\Game.uproject"
- UBT builds a project outside the declared projectPath

## Expected impact
Operators see a 400 instead of a build against the wrong project; could break a real project whose name contains a hyphen if UE ever allowed one (it does not for new projects).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - preflight only ever targets the declared project
Before: 3 of 3 crafted names (`..\\x`, `-Mode=Foo`, `a/b`) reach spawnCapture (walked against route.ts:62-125)
After: 0 of 3 predicted; the name rule must be confirmed against UE project-name constraints first
Method: simulation - walked the three names through the route; not built because the accepted alphabet needs confirming against existing operator projects
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
src/app/api/packaging/preflight/route.ts:44 typeof o.projectName === 'string'
src/app/api/packaging/preflight/route.ts:62 const uproject = path.join(req.projectPath, `${req.projectName}.uproject`)
src/app/api/packaging/preflight/route.ts:122 const target = isShipping ? request.projectName : `${request.projectName}Editor`
instrument: extend src/__tests__/api/packaging-preflight-route.test.ts with the three crafted names asserting 400 + spawnCapture not called, plus the real project names from projectStore recent projects asserting 200

title: Report a timed-out UBT or DataValidation run as a timeout
body:
## Summary
spawnCapture kills the child on timeout but resolves with spawnError null, so a 10/15-minute timeout reads as an ordinary parse failure.

## Description
src/lib/packaging/process-utils.ts:57 `setTimeout(kill, timeoutMs)` then the exit handler resolves `{ output, spawnError: null }`. The preflight route (src/app/api/packaging/preflight/route.ts:108-140) then runs parseUbtResult on truncated output and reports "fail" with whatever error lines happened to be captured, never the reason "timed out after 10 min". Fixed = SpawnCaptureResult carries `timedOut: true` and the route emits a fail detail naming the timeout. Out of this round's paths (process-utils is lib/packaging).

## Flow
- preflight build-verify-editor on a cold project exceeds UBT_TIMEOUT_MS
- timer kills UBT; exit resolves spawnError null
- route reports a generic build failure with no timeout reason

## Expected impact
An operator whose build timed out is told it failed to compile and goes hunting for a compiler error that does not exist.

## Evaluation
Claim: observability - timeouts are named
Before: 0 of 1 timeout paths name the timeout (read process-utils.ts:57-79)
After: 1 of 1 predicted
Method: simulation - traced the kill path; a fake spawnFn that never exits would measure it
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/lib/packaging/process-utils.ts:57 const timer = timeoutMs ? setTimeout(kill, timeoutMs) : undefined;
src/lib/packaging/process-utils.ts:75 child.once('exit', () => { cleanup(); resolve({ output, spawnError: null }); });
instrument: unit test with an injected spawnFn whose child never exits, timeoutMs=10, asserting the result names the timeout

title: Isolate instrumentation hooks so one failure cannot disarm the others
body:
## Summary
register() sets the started flag, then awaits imports and calls registerGateNotifier outside any try; a throw there skips the nightly cron and the drain worker for the life of the process.

## Description
src/instrumentation.ts:26 sets `__pofSchedulerStarted = true` before the Promise.all import (instrumentation.ts:28-34) and the unguarded registerGateNotifier() (instrumentation.ts:37). If either throws, register() rejects, setInterval is never armed, the drain-worker block never runs, and the flag prevents any HMR retry. The tick body and drain block already have their own try/catch — the gate notifier is the one hook without one. Fixed = wrap registerGateNotifier in try/logger.warn and set the flag only after the cron is armed.

## Flow
- gate-notifier import or eventBus.on throws at boot
- register() rejects before setInterval
- nightly builds and request_log purge silently never run; flag blocks retry

## Expected impact
Nightly builds keep running even when the webhook listener breaks; nothing visible changes on a healthy boot.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - hooks fail independently
Before: 1 throwing hook disables 3 of 3 hooks (walked instrumentation.ts:22-81)
After: 1 of 3 predicted
Method: simulation - the Before requires an injected throw; a vitest with mocked dynamic imports would measure it
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vitest: NEXT_RUNTIME=nodejs, vi.mock gate-notifier to throw, fake timers; assert tickScheduler called after one scheduleTick

title: Bound crash-log import size before parsing, not only at storage
body:
## Summary
POST /api/crash-analyzer parse-log parses the whole pasted rawText before crash history truncates it to 64 KB.

## Description
src/app/api/crash-analyzer/route.ts parse-log passes rawText straight to parseCrashLog (src/lib/crash-analyzer/crash-log-parser.ts:67-68 splits every line, then regex-scans the whole text) and analyzeSingleCrash; truncation to CRASH_HISTORY_LIMITS.rawLogChars (src/types/crash-analyzer.ts:71-74) only happens inside recordCrashSighting. A pasted multi-MB editor log is split and scanned in full on the request thread. Fixed = cap the parse window (e.g. the crash section, or N x rawLogChars) and say so; never reject a real log outright.

## Flow
- operator pastes a whole Saved/Logs file (tens of MB)
- route splits and scans every line synchronously
- only then truncates to 64 KB for storage

## Expected impact
Large pastes return faster and do not stall the Node event loop; a cap that drops the crash section would mis-parse, so the window must be taken from the crash marker.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - parse cost bounded by the stored window
Before: unmeasured; parse is O(rawText) with no ceiling (read route.ts + crash-log-parser.ts:67-82)
After: O(cap) predicted
Method: simulation - a timing probe at 1/10/50 MB through parseCrashLog would take both figures; not run this round (budget)
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: timing probe: parseCrashLog + analyzeSingleCrash on a synthetic 1/10/50 MB log, before and after the window cap

title: Guard lookupJargon against Object.prototype keys (pair of the crash-glossary fix)
body:
## Summary
blueprint-jargon lookupJargon still returns inherited members for toString / __proto__ / constructor; crash-glossary was fixed this round, its base dictionary was not.

## Description
src/lib/blueprint-jargon.ts:340-342 `return ALL_JARGON[term]` on a plain object literal. lookupCrashTerm now filters the fallback (commit 5094ddc3), but every other consumer of lookupJargon (TermChip, findJargonInText callers) still gets a function back for `toString`. Fixed = `Object.hasOwn(ALL_JARGON, term) ? ALL_JARGON[term] : undefined`. Out of this round's paths.

## Flow
- a blueprint/UI string contains the token toString
- lookupJargon returns Object.prototype.toString
- tooltip renders "undefined"

## Expected impact
No stray "undefined" tooltips on jargon chips; nothing else changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - only real glossary entries resolve
Before: 7 of 7 prototype tokens resolve (same probe as crash-glossary-prototype-keys.test.ts, applied to the base dictionary)
After: 0 of 7 predicted
Method: probe - the crash-glossary test proved the class; this half is in another context's file
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Honour reduced motion in the crash detail and raw-log disclosures
body:
## Summary
3 of 5 Framer motion sites in the crash views animate height without consulting useReducedMotion, while the detail slide and the Time Machine do.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/CrashAnalyzerView/CrashDetailPanel.tsx:111, PatternCard.tsx:58 and RawLog.tsx:38 run `initial={{height:0}} animate={{height:"auto"}}` unconditionally. index.tsx:295 and CrashTimeMachine/index.tsx:155 route through motionSafe(…, prefersReducedMotion). Fixed = the same useReducedMotion + motionSafe pattern (reference_reduced_motion_pattern).

## Flow
- user with prefers-reduced-motion opens "Show technical details"
- panel height tweens anyway
- other crash motion on the same screen is suppressed

## Expected impact
Vestibular-sensitive users get an instant disclosure; no visible change for everyone else.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - reduced-motion honoured on every crash-analyzer motion site
Before: 2 of 5 sites honour it (grep motion. + useReducedMotion over CrashAnalyzerView/ and CrashTimeMachine/)
After: 5 of 5 predicted
Method: simulation - framer in jsdom needs a mocked useReducedMotion and a transition assertion; not built this round
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: component test mocking useReducedMotion=true and asserting the motion.div transition duration is 0 for all three disclosures

title: Surface why a Bridge Doctor restore preview failed
body:
## Summary
previewRestore swallows the probe error and returns to idle, so a failed dry-probe leaves no reason anywhere.

## Description
src/stores/bridgeDoctorStore.ts:145-148 `catch { set({ restorePhase: "idle", restorePreview: null }); return null; }`. The caller cannot distinguish "already running" (the guard at :128 also returns null) from "the probe threw", and the error text is discarded. Fixed = keep a `restoreError` string (non-persisted) set in the catch and cleared on the next preview, rendered by the restore UI.

## Flow
- operator clicks Preview restore
- probe throws (port refused, bad host)
- UI drops back to idle with no message

## Expected impact
Operators learn why the known-good config could not be checked; partialize keeps the new field out of localStorage.

## Evaluation
Claim: observability - preview failures carry a reason
Before: 0 of 2 null-return paths say why (read bridgeDoctorStore.ts:126-149)
After: 2 of 2 predicted
Method: simulation - the store is testable with an injected throwing probe (bridgeDoctorRestore.store.test.ts already injects probes)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/stores/bridgeDoctorStore.ts:128 if (st.running || st.restorePhase === 'previewing') return null;
src/stores/bridgeDoctorStore.ts:145 } catch {
instrument: extend src/__tests__/components/bridge-doctor/bridgeDoctorRestore.store.test.ts with a rejecting probe asserting restoreError is set

title: Stop persisting a second copy of the bridge auth token
body:
## Summary
bridgeDoctorStore persists lastKnownGood.authToken to localStorage key pof-bridge-doctor, duplicating the token pofBridgeStore already persists.

## Description
src/stores/bridgeDoctorStore.ts:114 copies report.config.authToken into lastKnownGood, and partialize (:173) writes it under pof-bridge-doctor; src/stores/pofBridgeStore.ts:95 already persists pofAuthToken. Two plaintext copies means rotating the token leaves the old one at rest until the next all-green run. Fixed = store a token fingerprint (or a "token unchanged" flag) in lastKnownGood and restore the token only when the live one still matches, or read it from pofBridgeStore at restore time.

## Flow
- operator rotates the PoF bridge token
- pof-bridge-doctor still holds the old token in localStorage
- restore can write the revoked token back

## Expected impact
One copy of the secret at rest; restore must still round-trip host/ports, which is what the existing restore tests pin.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one persisted copy of the bridge secret
Before: 2 localStorage keys hold the token (read partialize in both stores)
After: 1 predicted
Method: simulation - needs a decision on restore semantics for the token before a test can pin it
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
src/stores/bridgeDoctorStore.ts:114 authToken: report.config.authToken ?? '',
src/stores/bridgeDoctorStore.ts:173 partialize: (state) => ({ lastKnownGood: state.lastKnownGood }),
src/stores/pofBridgeStore.ts:95 pofAuthToken: state.pofAuthToken,
instrument: store test asserting JSON in localStorage["pof-bridge-doctor"] has no authToken while bridgeDoctorRestore.store.test.ts stays green

title: Replace sub-AA opacity text in BlueprintInspector with --text-subtle
body:
## Summary
BlueprintInspector uses text-text-muted/50 for the empty-state hint and EmptyHint hint lines — the legibility guard baselines 3 text sites + 1 icon here.

## Description
src/components/modules/project-setup/BlueprintInspector/index.tsx:182 and primitives.tsx:29 use `text-text-muted/50`; index.tsx:98 uses `placeholder:text-text-muted/50`. src/__tests__/a11y/legibility-floor-guard.test.ts:154-155 baselines {index: text 2, icons 1; primitives: text 1}. Fixed = text-text-subtle (≥4.5:1 per globals.css:26), then the director lowers those baseline rows after the wave run.

## Flow
- operator opens Blueprint Inspector with no path
- hint line renders at ~50% of muted text — below AA
- same in every empty section hint

## Expected impact
Hint text becomes readable; the ratchet must be lowered by the director (shared file).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - hint text meets AA
Before: 3 sub-AA text sites (legibility-floor-guard baseline rows)
After: 0 predicted
Method: gate - the guard counts them, but lowering its baseline is director-owned per the brief, so not landed in-round
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: legibility-floor-guard.test.ts with the two baseline rows lowered

title: Drop the redundant home-directory listing on PathBrowser fresh mount
body:
## Summary
getHomeDir lists the entire home directory only to read its resolved path, then the hook lists the suggested folder — 3 POSTs on a fresh mount where 2 suffice.

## Description
src/components/modules/project-setup/PathBrowser/helpers.ts:3-13 POSTs {action:"list", path:"~"} and discards everything but data.path; usePathBrowser.ts:87 awaits it before browse(suggestions[0]). On a home directory with many entries this is a full readdir + .uproject probe per child for one string. Fixed = a `home` action (or the detect-engines answer carrying homeDir) on /api/filesystem/browse, which is outside these paths.

## Flow
- Start fresh opens PathBrowser
- detect-engines, list ~, list Documents\\Unreal Projects
- the ~ listing is thrown away

## Expected impact
One fewer filesystem scan per wizard open; route change is in another context.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - fewer filesystem scans per mount
Before: 3 browse POSTs on a startFresh mount (counted in usePathBrowser.race.test-style mock)
After: 2 predicted
Method: simulation - needs a server action outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/project-setup/PathBrowser/helpers.ts:8 body: JSON.stringify({ action: 'list', path: '~' }),
src/components/modules/project-setup/PathBrowser/usePathBrowser.ts:87 const homeDir = await getHomeDir();
instrument: renderHook with a counting apiFetch mock over a startFresh mount, before and after
